newsitem.title: CHINA: China warns against resurging bigamy, concubines.
newsitem.headline: China warns against resurging bigamy, concubines.

text.p: A top Chinese women's official on Wednesday warned of a resurgence of bigamy and the taking of concubines, saying such practices were uncivilised and harmed women and families.

Bigamy and concubinage, abolished after the Communist Party swept to power in 1949, had made a comeback in recent years as broad economic reforms freed people from once-firm government control, the China Women's News quoted Huang Qizao, secretary of the All-China Women's Federation, as saying.

"Multiple wives and the taking of concubines is a horrible practice left over from feudal society, (it) takes discrimination against and dallying with women as its premises and is a serious violation of socialist ethics," Huang was quoted as saying.
Many businessmen, especially in booming eastern coastal regions, have secretly married women in different cities or conceal lovers whom they keep as virtual concubines far from home.

"Multiple marriages and the taking of concubines is an illegal activity undertaken by a small number of uneducated people who have suddenly become rich and who have no regard for the law," Huang said.

Some cases of multiple marriage had resulted in threats to public security, she added, but did not elaborate. However, Chinese media often carry reports of murder and arson attacks carried out by jilted wives or dissatisfied lovers.
"Multiple marriages and the taking of concubines not only disrupt marriages and families but harm the rights and interests of women," Huang said.
Bigamy violated the constitution, the Marriage Law and the Criminal Law, she said, adding that the problem should be dealt with in a comprehensive manner.

The Communist Party, families and the media should all join the fight against bigamy and concubinage and authorities should use the law, administrative measures and education to help to wipe out the vogue, she said.
"No matter whether in the home, at the workplace or in society, we must create a ... public opinion environment where this kind of ugly phenomenon cannot propagate and spread," Huang said.
China has also tried to fight a rampant slave trade in women who are kidnapped and sold off as wives or concubines to men in distant villages.
The traditional Confucian preference for sons has been blamed for making it more difficult for some men to find wives by encouraging female infanticide.
